newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GERMAN HOLIDAY HELPS OLO/BUND SPREAD HIT NEW LOW.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN HOLIDAY HELPS OLO/BUND SPREAD HIT NEW LOW.

text.p: Belgian bond futures finished firmer and OLOs were steady on Thursday, with the 10-year yield premium over German Bunds edging in further to a historic low of nine basis points compared to 12 on Wednesday.
The 2006 OLO yield ended at an unchanged 6.14 percent.
Dealers noted, though, that the spread narrowing had been made easier by a bank holiday in Germany and predicted it would slip back into double figures again on Friday.
One dealer, who had forecast a lower spread in coming months as the single European currency neared, said, "Everything is being anticipated two years earlier than expected."

Another said the market was forgetting that a single currency did not mean the yields should be at par because Belgium would still have a greater credit risk than Germany. He thought this could be reflected in a yield premium of 20 bps.
December OLO futures ended 13 bps up at 119.15 after hitting a contract high of 119.20 when the U.S. market fell out of bed. Profit-taking ate into Initial gains in Treasuries.
All eyes will now be on Friday's monthly U.S. jobs data with OLOs seen rangebound until the data are published at 1230 GMT.
